newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb gets court order against AgrEvo.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb gets court order against AgrEvo.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Friday that the U.S. Federal District Court in Chicago issued a restraining order against AgrEvo USA Co.

The order prohibits AgrEvo from making allegedly false and misleading statements to farmers concerning the use of AgrEvo's Liberty glufosinate herbicide on DeKalb's corn hybrids that have been genetically altered to resist use of glufosinate herbicides.
Liberty is a trademark of Hoechst Schering AgrEvo GmbH, which is a venture between Hoechst AG and Schering AG.

DeKalb said the order, issued by the court on Thursday, prohibits AgrEvo from allegedly telling farmers or herbicide applicators that it is illegal to apply Liberty herbicide to DeKalb's new GR (glufosinate resistant) corn hybrids.
The order is the latest development in a dispute between AgrEvo and DeKalb regarding the Liberty herbicide and DeKalb's corn hybrids.

Hoechst Schering AgrEvo sued DeKalb Genetics for alleged infringement of its Liberty herbicide trademark. In papers filed in Delaware Chancery Court this week, the venture sought an order barring DeKalb from using the Liberty trademark with its products, specifically seed corn.

DeKalb's corn is among the crops that have been genetically altered to resist the use of certain herbicides. This allows farmers to spray their fields with the herbicides to kill weeds without harming the crop.

"This restraining order confirms what DeKalb has been telling farmers all winter," Richard Ryan, DeKalb president, said in a statement. "There are no restrictions on the application of Liberty herbicide to DeKalb's GR corn hybrids."
